title: Enhanced interfacial charge-transfer kinetics and power densities in noble metal-decorated ZnO nanorods for asymmetric supercapacitors
content: This work reports the first systematic investigation of noble metal-decorated ZnO (M = Ag, Au, and Pt) nanorods as potential electrode materials for supercapacitor applications. Synthesised via a facile hydrothermal route, the nanorods were characterised by structural and chemical analyses (XRD, TEM, XPS), confirming a crystalline hexagonal wurtzite framework (P63mc) decorated with metallic Ag, Au and Pt nanoparticles. The b-values obtained from Dunn's kinetic analysis were 0.6 and 0.7, revealing hybrid surface-induced capacitive and diffusion-controlled intercalation processes. The symmetric Pt-decorated ZnO (ZPT) cell achieved a maximal specific capacitance (Cs) of 86.4 F g−1 at 1.5 A g−1. The system also delivered an energy density (Ed) of 7.8 Wh kg−1 at a corresponding power density (Pd) of 1203 W kg−1, while retaining 95.82% of capacitance across 10 000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Meanwhile, the hybrid ZPT//ZAU supercapacitor attained Cs of 62.6 F g−1, highlighting that the ZPT electrode delivers 1.38-fold higher capacitance under the same circumstances, supported by a low solution resistance (Rs = 1.0 Ω). A symmetric ZPT CR2032 coin cell exhibits an Ed of 0.7 Wh kg−1 at 0.05 A g−1. As a qualitative proof of concept, the assembled device illuminated a commercial red LED for about 20 s after 300 s of charging.
